parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of EnrolmentsService is about enrolment: enrolling and withdrawing a student, using its own Repository<EnrolmentEntity>. That part is fine. The problem is that it also injects `@InjectRepository(CourseEntity) courseRepository` and writes course data itself. In `enrol` it loads the course row, borrows the `toCourse` mapping function from courses.service.ts, then copies `course.enrolled` back onto the row by hand and calls `courseRepository.save(entity)`. So it uses half of the courses module's abstraction (the row-to-Course mapper) and skips the rest, saving course rows directly. That means the rule for saving a Course and mapping it back to a row now lives here as well as wherever the courses module keeps it. Course persistence is a different concern from enrolment, and this service goes around the courses module's boundary to do it. The candidate flag (one I/O category plus three other components: the course repository, the courses mapper and the domain types) matches this: the service's dependencies spread into the courses module's persistence. Possible duplication of the email check (`includes('@')`) elsewhere can't be confirmed from the source given, so I don't count it.
